#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract hardirq handler -> plain-lock pairs and cross-index with non-handler plain lock sites."""
import re, os, sys, json, collections

S = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s08"
regs = []
with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "irq_regs.txt")) as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        m = re.match(r'^(.*?):(\d+):(.*)$', line)
        if not m: continue
        path, lineno, text = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
        regs.append((path, lineno, text))

# Handler name: the identifier that appears in the first non-string argument position after (irq, handler
# Typical: request_irq(irq, handler, flags, "name", dev) ; request_threaded_irq(irq, thread_fn? no: (irq, handler, thread_fn, flags...)
handler_re = re.compile(r'(?:devm_)?request(?:_threaded)?_irq\s*\(')

def parse_handler(text, kind):
    """Return list of candidate handler identifiers (positional 1st fn for request_irq/devm; 1st fn for threaded)."""
    m = handler_re.search(text)
    if not m: return []
    inner = text[m.end():]
    # strip trailing context beyond balanced parens
    depth = 1; i = 0; out = ''
    instr = False; esc = False; inchr = False
    while i < len(inner) and depth > 0:
        c = inner[i]
        if instr:
            if esc: esc = False
            elif c == '\\': esc = True
            elif c == '"': instr = False
            out += c
        elif inchr:
            if esc: esc = False
            elif c == '\\': esc = True
            elif c == "'": inchr = False
            out += c
        else:
            if c == '"': instr = True; out += c
            elif c == "'": inchr = True; out += c
            elif c == '(': depth += 1; out += c
            elif c == ')': depth -= 1
                if depth == 0: break
                out += c
            else: out += c
        i += 1
    args = []
    cur = ''; d2 = 0; instr2 = False; esc2 = False
    for c in out:
        if instr2:
            cur += c
            if esc2: esc2 = False
            elif c == '\\': esc2 = True
            elif c == '"': instr2 = False
            continue
        if c == '"':
            instr2 = True; cur += c; continue
        if c in '([': d2 += 1
        if c in ')]': d2 -= 1
        if c == ',' and d2 == 0:
            args.append(cur.strip()); cur = ''
        else:
            cur += c
    if cur.strip(): args.append(cur.strip())
    if not args: return []
    # first argument that looks like a function identifier or NULL
    def is_fn(a):
        a = a.strip()
        if a in ('NULL',): return None
        if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', a): return a
        return None
    if kind in ('request_irq', 'devm_request_irq'):
        h = is_fn(args[1]) if len(args) > 1 else None
        return [h] if h else []
    else:  # threaded
        out_ids = []
        if len(args) > 1 and is_fn(args[1]): out_ids.append(is_fn(args[1]))
        if len(args) > 2 and is_fn(args[2]): out_ids.append(is_fn(args[2]))
        return [x for x in out_ids if x]

results = []
for path, lineno, text in regs:
    kind = None
    if 'request_threaded_irq' in text: kind = 'threaded'
    elif 'devm_request_irq' in text: kind = 'devm_request_irq'
    elif 'request_irq' in text: kind = 'request_irq'
    else: continue
    hs = parse_handler(text, kind)
    results.append({'path': path, 'line': lineno, 'kind': kind, 'handlers': hs, 'text': text.strip()})

# Load file contents
filecache = {}
def get_file(path):
    if path not in filecache:
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(S, path), errors='replace') as f:
                filecache[path] = f.read().splitlines()
        except OSError:
            filecache[path] = None
    return filecache[path]

def find_funcs(lines, name):
    """Return (start,end) line ranges (1-based inclusive) of definitions of function `name`."""
    ranges = []
    pat = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ \t\*&]*\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\(')
    n = len(lines)
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if pat.match(l):
            # walk to find opening brace and matching close
            j = i
            # find '{' within next 15 lines
            k = j
            while k < n and k < j + 15:
                if '{' in lines[k]: break
                if ';' in lines[k] and k == j: break  # prototype on one line
                k += 1
            if k >= n or k >= j + 15 or '{' not in lines[k]: continue
            depth = 0; started = False
            m2 = k
            while m2 < n:
                depth += lines[m2].count('{') - lines[m2].count('}')
                if depth > 0: started = True
                if started and depth <= 0:
                    ranges.append((j + 1, m2 + 1))
                    break
                m2 += 1
    return ranges

lock_acq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')
lock_irq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(')

pairs = []  # (path, regline, handler, kind, handler_def_range, acq_line, lock_expr)
unresolved = []
for r in results:
    for h in r['handlers']:
        lines = get_file(r['path'])
        if lines is None: continue
        rngs = find_funcs(lines, h)
        if not rngs:
            unresolved.append((r['path'], r['line'], h, r['kind']))
            continue
        for (a, b) in rngs:
            for ln in range(a, b + 1):
                if ln - 1 >= len(lines): break
                l = lines[ln - 1]
                if lock_irq.search(l): 
                    # skip lines that also have plain? irqsave wins for that line
                    continue
                for m in lock_acq.finditer(l):
                    pairs.append({'path': r['path'], 'regline': r['line'], 'handler': h,
                                  'kind': r['kind'], 'func_start': a, 'func_end': b,
                                  'acq_line': ln, 'lock': m.group(1)})

with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "handler_plain_locks.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(pairs, f, indent=1)
with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "unresolved_handlers.txt"), "w") as f:
    for u in unresolved:
        f.write("%s\n" % (u,))
print("registrations:", len(results))
print("handler-plain-lock acquisitions:", len(pairs))
print("distinct handler lock exprs:", len(set(p['lock'] for p in pairs)))
print("unresolved handlers:", len(set(u[2] for u in unresolved)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cross-index handler-plain locks with plain spin_lock sites elsewhere in the same file (outside the handler function)."""
import re, os, json, collections

W = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
S = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s08"
pairs = json.load(open(os.path.join(W, "handler_plain_locks.json")))

filecache = {}
def get_file(path):
    if path not in filecache:
        with open(os.path.join(S, path), errors='replace') as f:
            filecache[path] = f.read().splitlines()
    return filecache[path]

lock_acq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')
lock_irq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(')
lock_bh  = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_bh\s*\(')

# normalize lock expression: strip whitespace
def norm(e):
    return re.sub(r'\s+', '', e)

by_file = collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in pairs:
    by_file[p['path']].append(p)

rows = []
for path, ps in by_file.items():
    lines = get_file(path)
    handler_ranges = set((p['handler'], p['func_start'], p['func_end']) for p in ps)
    hlocks = set(norm(p['lock']) for p in ps)
    hfuncs = set(p['handler'] for p in ps)
    # find all plain spin_lock sites outside handler bodies
    other_plain = []
    n = len(lines)
    # compute function ranges per line using simple heuristic: track via find_funcs for all handlers only; for other lines, classify by context markers
    for ln in range(1, n + 1):
        l = lines[ln - 1]
        if lock_irq.search(l) or lock_bh.search(l):
            continue
        for m in lock_acq.finditer(l):
            e = norm(m.group(1))
            if e in hlocks:
                in_handler = False
                for (h, a, b) in handler_ranges:
                    if a <= ln <= b:
                        in_handler = True
                        break
                if not in_handler:
                    other_plain.append((ln, e, l.strip()))
    if other_plain:
        rows.append({'path': path, 'handler_locks': sorted(hlocks), 'handlers': sorted(hfuncs),
                     'handler_sites': [(p['handler'], p['acq_line'], p['lock'], p['regline'], p['kind']) for p in ps],
                     'other_plain': other_plain})

rows.sort(key=lambda r: -len(r['other_plain']))
with open(os.path.join(W, "cross.tsv.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(rows, f, indent=1)
for r in rows[:40]:
    print(f"{r['path']} handlers={r['handlers']} hlocks={r['handler_locks']} other_plain={len(r['other_plain'])}")
print("files with candidate pairs:", len(rows))

content.thinking:
Confirmed: mtk_star_emac.c in s08 shows:
- hardirq handler `mtk_star_handle_irq` (registered at line 1002 via request_irq presumably) takes `spin_lock(&priv->lock)` at line 783 (plain).
- NAPI poll callbacks `mtk_star_tx_poll` (around line 1185-1186) and `mtk_star_rx_poll` (line 1351-1352) take `spin_lock(&priv->lock)` plainly.

NAPI poll runs in softirq (NET_RX) context with hard IRQs enabled. So a hardirq can preempt the NAPI poll on the same CPU while the poll holds priv->lock, and the hardirq handler spins forever on that lock — the preempted softirq can never resume. This is a hardirq-vs-softirq deadlock. The hardirq preempts softirq (hardirqs are enabled during NAPI softirq processing), so it's a genuine deadlock.

Let me verify the request_irq site and check for any irqsave usage of priv->lock anywhere in the file.

  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",

  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c

-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);

-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cross-index handler-plain locks with plain spin_lock sites elsewhere in the same file (outside the handler function)."""
import re, os, json, collections

W = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
S = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s08"
pairs = json.load(open(os.path.join(W, "handler_plain_locks.json")))

filecache = {}
def get_file(path):
    if path not in filecache:
        with open(os.path.join(S, path), errors='replace') as f:
            filecache[path] = f.read().splitlines()
    return filecache[path]

lock_acq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')
lock_irq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(')
lock_bh  = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_bh\s*\(')

# normalize lock expression: strip whitespace
def norm(e):
    return re.sub(r'\s+', '', e)

by_file = collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in pairs:
    by_file[p['path']].append(p)

rows = []
for path, ps in by_file.items():
    lines = get_file(path)
    handler_ranges = set((p['handler'], p['func_start'], p['func_end']) for p in ps)
    hlocks = set(norm(p['lock']) for p in ps)
    hfuncs = set(p['handler'] for p in ps)
    # find all plain spin_lock sites outside handler bodies
    other_plain = []
    n = len(lines)
    # compute function ranges per line using simple heuristic: track via find_funcs for all handlers only; for other lines, classify by context markers
    for ln in range(1, n + 1):
        l = lines[ln - 1]
        if lock_irq.search(l) or lock_bh.search(l):
            continue
        for m in lock_acq.finditer(l):
            e = norm(m.group(1))
            if e in hlocks:
                in_handler = False
                for (h, a, b) in handler_ranges:
                    if a <= ln <= b:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cross-index handler-plain locks with plain spin_lock sites elsewhere in the same file (outside the handler function)."""
import re, os, json, collections

W = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
S = "/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C7/public/snapshots/s08"
pairs = json.load(open(os.path.join(W, "handler_plain_locks.json")))

filecache = {}
def get_file(path):
    if path not in filecache:
        with open(os.path.join(S, path), errors='replace') as f:
            filecache[path] = f.read().splitlines()
    return filecache[path]

lock_acq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock\s*\(\s*([^);]+?)\s*\)')
lock_irq = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_irq(?:save)?\s*\(')
lock_bh  = re.compile(r'\bspin_lock_bh\s*\(')

# normalize lock expression: strip whitespace
def norm(e):
    return re.sub(r'\s+', '', e)

by_file = collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in pairs:
    by_file[p['path']].append(p)

rows = []
for path, ps in by_file.items():
    lines = get_file(path)
    handler_ranges = set((p['handler'], p['func_start'], p['func_end']) for p in ps)
    hlocks = set(norm(p['lock']) for p in ps)
    hfuncs = set(p['handler'] for p in ps)
    # find all plain spin_lock sites outside handler bodies
    other_plain = []
    n = len(lines)
    # compute function ranges per line using simple heuristic: track via find_funcs for all handlers only; for other lines, classify by context markers
    for ln in range(1, n + 1):
        l = lines[ln - 1]
        if lock_irq.search(l) or lock_bh.search(l):
            continue
        for m in lock_acq.finditer(l):
            e = norm(m.group(1))
            if e in hlocks:
                in_handler = False
                for (h, a, b) in handler_ranges:
                    if a <= ln <= b:
                        in_handler = True
                        break
                if not in_handler:
                    other_plain.append((ln, e, l.strip()))
    if other_plain:
        rows.append({'path': path, 'handler_locks': sorted(hlocks), 'handlers': sorted(hfuncs),
                     'handler_sites': [(p['handler'], p['acq_line'], p['lock'], p['regline'], p['kind']) for p in ps],
                     'other_plain': other_plain})

rows.sort(key=lambda r: -len(r['other_plain']))
with open(os.path.join(W, "cross.tsv.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(rows, f, indent=1)
for r in rows[:40]:
    print(f"{r['path']} handlers={r['handlers']} hlocks={r['handler_locks']} other_plain={len(r['other_plain'])}")
print("files with candidate pairs:", len(rows))

{
  "hexsha": "058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018",
  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",
  "vulnerability_summary": "tx_dev_lock is acquired with spin_lock() in process context via workqueue path, but the same lock is acquired in xmit callback running under softirq/timer context, causing a deadlock due to missing bottom-half disabling.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Plain spin_lock used for data shared between process context and softirq/timer callback context, violating the invariant that softirq-safe locks must disable bottom halves.",
  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018\nAuthor: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>\nDate:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000\n\n    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock\n    \n    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which\n    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()\n    on it to prevent potential deadlock.\n    \n    hostif_sme_work()\n    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()\n    --> hostif_mib_set_request()\n    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()\n    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)\n    \n    ks_wlan_start_xmit()\n    --> hostif_data_request()\n    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()\n    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)\n    \n    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>\n    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com\n    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>\n\ndiff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c\nindex 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644\n--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c\n+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c\n@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,\n \tpriv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);\n \tpriv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;\n \n-\tspin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);\n+\tspin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);\n \tresult = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);\n-\tspin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);\n+\tspin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);\n \n \tif (txq_has_space(priv))\n \t\tqueue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);\n"
}
